Strengths
- Clear separation of concerns: data ingestion, analysis engine, and reporting interfaces.
- Containerized, stateless services enable predictable deployments and rollbacks.
- Baseline observability (centralized logs, metrics) and health checks in place.
- Versioned schemas and immutable analysis artifacts support reproducibility.

Weaknesses
- Analysis engine tightly coupled to orchestration; changes propagate broadly.
- Long-running analyses exposed via synchronous APIs; poor UX and timeouts.
- Data validation inconsistent; limited lineage and provenance tracking.
- Horizontal scaling constrained for CPU/GPU-intensive workloads.
- Gaps in test coverage (performance, integration) and capacity planning.

Recommendations
- Decouple execution with an asynchronous job model: enqueue analyses (e.g., Kafka/SQS), idempotent workers, and a job/status API with callbacks; use event-driven orchestration to isolate components.
- Formalize data contracts and lineage: enforce schema validation (e.g., Great Expectations), track lineage (OpenLineage/Marquez), and store versioned inputs/outputs in an artifact registry to guarantee reproducibility.
- Define SLOs (latency, throughput, success rate) and implement performance testing with representative workloads; add autoscaling policies (HPA/KEDA), resource quotas, and scheduling for CPU/GPU pools; integrate cost and utilization dashboards to guide capacity and optimization.
